correctness.rationale: For nonzero \(f=x^s u\) and \(g=u h\), the bracket identity cancels all derivatives of the unit \(u\), reducing the centralizer equation to \(h'=0\) for \(s=0\) and to \(x^{s-1}(x h'-s h)=0\) for \(s\ge1\). Coefficient comparison gives exactly \(s-1\) unconstrained high-degree coordinates plus one additional coordinate precisely when \(2s\le p\). Valuation-stratum sizes then give the multiplicities, and summing \(q^{\dim C_W(D)}\) gives \(q^{p-2}(q^3+((p-1)/2)(q^2-1))\). The packaged checker exhaustively verifies \(W_1(\mathbb F_5)\) and representative non-monomial cases in characteristics \(7\) and \(11\).

value.rationale: The claim gives a natural complete finite-field invariant for the basic one-variable Jacobson–Witt algebra: every element-centralizer size, its exact multiplicity, and the resulting commutativity degree. The valuation transition at \(s=(p-1)/2\) explains the nonequidimensional centralizer behavior and quantifies the regular locus. This is a structurally motivated classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical table.
